thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: Triggered alert inference.latency.p95.prod (threshold 800ms) — 5 pages across prod-eu/prod-us-east/prod-apac. Alert grouped into PD: SRE-Primary.

jamie: ack'd the PD page, I'm looking. any customer tickets?

pd-bot: PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged by jamie. If unacknowledged in 5m, will escalate to SRE-Secondary.

matt: seeing a short burst of p95 ~1.2s on the inference fleet. No 5xx spike. % of affected requests ~0.6%.

tanvi: I can confirm increased tail on model-x-small routes, looks like a cold-KV warmup pattern but weird it's across regions at once.

leah: did any deploys land ~11:20? I don't see any from deploy-bot.

oncall-backup: no deploys from infra or runtime in the last 30m.

jamie: running quick query on routing logs to see if traffic got routed to higher latency hosts.

jamie: (logs)
```
> rlog query --since 5m "route:inference AND p95>800" --group-by host
host-12-prod-east: 120ms p95
host-47-prod-eu: 1.1s p95
host-88-prod-apac: 980ms p95
```

matt: hmmm host-12 looks fine. host-47/88 show the spike. Not consistent with a single regional outage.

infra-eng: checking infra metrics on GPU utilization and network. nothing crazy in CPU or NIC.

jamie: I see a scheduled loadtest job (infra/canary/loadgen) kicked off at 11:19 accidentally in prod-eu and prod-apac — the canary job namespace name matches. Could be noisy.

cust-success: product team reports one minor customer complaint about slowed chat responses at 11:21 but they said it recovered in ~2m. No rate-limiting errors.

tanvi: if it's the loadgen canary hitting multiple regions, that's likely the common denominator. let's throttle or kill it and watch.

leah: +1. matt, can you pause canary in those regions? command below.

matt: pausing canary jobs now.
```
> k -n canary-prod-eu delete job/loadgen-2026-11-19-1120 --grace-period=0
> k -n canary-prod-apac delete job/loadgen-2026-11-19-1120 --grace-period=0
```

matt: deleted.

incident-bot: Alert inference.latency.p95.prod resolved (auto-resolve by alerting system) — no further pages.

jamie: seeing p95 back to normal across regions in the next 90s.

tanvi: quick verification: run a short synthetic across model-x-small route.

jamie: synthetic run result: p95=210ms, error rate 0.00%.

oncall-backup: looks like transient noise from the canary. No rollback or config changes needed.

leah: re: customer impact — small blip, one complaint, no errors or data loss. recommend mark as "no customer-impact" with note.

matt: adding a tag to the canary infra job so it doesn't auto-run in prod without manual approval. filed infra PR: https://internal.redwood/infrastructure/pull/582 (linking).

jamie: assigning follow-up to infra-eng to add a safety check on canary scheduler and notify product when canaries run in prod.

infra-eng: noted, will add scheduler gating + slack notif. ETA tomorrow EOD.

pd-bot: PagerDuty: Incident closed by jamie.

jamie: handing off to tanvi for post-incident doc/ops note. I'll update status in incident tracker. :white_check_mark:

tanvi: will write short postmortem note: root cause = accidental prod canary loadgen across regions causing transient tail latency, auto-resolved after job kill, customer impact = minimal. Will include action items (scheduler gating, PR link, add runbook step to pause canaries).

cust-success: pinged affected customer, they confirmed recovery and are good with note. :thumbsup:

leah: nice quick catch and clear. closing thread.

jamie: :party-parrot: good team work.
